items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Benny Goodman’s band, and some of the earlier bands were working a lot.

ctx.x: What was the work scene like for that band and that style of music. Those were tough years weren’t they?

How much did the band work. The band probably didn’t work as much as the bands during the 40s worked. They were out — Benny Goodman’s band, and some of the earlier bands were working a lot. Mulligan would do weekends at a club in Jersey perhaps, or he’d do something in Upstate New York, he’d do some run outs from New York. We did a couple of tours. We toured this country and it was mainly one-nighters. We went to Europe. We were busy in Europe. But sporadic would have to be the word. Because there were times when…
What kind of money were you making with that group?
